chapter: Depression gigs, Lil Armstrong, joining Chick Webb
title: Gigging with Elmer Snowden and other contractors
summary: After the Club Kentucky McRae worked jobs for contractors like Elmer Snowden, who ran several bands in hotels and on Long Island on the same night.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Getting paid: wages, scale and the pay envelope

blocks.x: How about your period with Elmer Snowden? You were largely with June Clark, but you also played also with Elmer. In other words, these were your gigs --
Yeah, these were the gigs with Elmer Snowden. I just gigged with Elmer Snowden, you know.

After the Club Kentucky gig was over with June Clark, we just went into another phrase of gigging around. (inaudible). This was leading up to the time when we doing all this -- you know, doing like gigging here and running here. Playing with this guy, Elmer Snowden, this guy. Whoever was the (inaudible) contractor. These guys like Elmer Snowden had -- they were like contractors for these gigs. Like, people would call them. Some of these guys, they had two or three bands they would send out. You know, they put together this band -- he's working on this job.
S. & S. REPORTING COMPANY, INC. WOrth 2-2915 WOrth 2-2943
Say, "Look, I want you to take care of this job." Got five pieces going here or Jersey or some place. Long Island or upstate New York.
And that -- just gigs. Maybe he'd play in a hotel. When they (inaudible) merged together, the colored musicians got a lot of -- this was important, because they got a lot of gigs.

They started playing these hotels. And sometimes Elmer and them guys (inaudible) had -- Elmer Snowden had like two or three bands working that same night. Friday night, Saturday night, (inaudible) Sunday, see. You'd be working.
When you go to the Rhythm Club, that's when the person was really hitting the (inaudible) bands.
